'''''Malus prunifolia''''' is a species of [[crabapple]]  tree known by the common names '''plumleaf crab apple''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=MAPR|taxon=Malus prunifolia|accessdate=27 January 2016}}</ref> '''plum-leaved apple''',<ref name="BSBI07">{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref> '''pear-leaf crabapple''', '''Chinese apple''' and '''Chinese crabapple'''.<ref name="hort">{{cite web |url=http://hortiplex.gardenweb.com/plants/nph-ind.cgi?name=Malus&f=d&gl=1&p=1 |title=Search results for: Malus |access-date=September 11, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100404011219/http://hortiplex.gardenweb.com/plants/nph-ind.cgi?name=Malus&f=d&gl=1&p=1 |archive-date=April 4, 2010 }}</ref> It is native to China.

The number of chromosomes is 2n = 34.<ref>
{{cite web |url=https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Chromosome-numbers-of-the-Malus-wild-species-collection-Dresden-Pillnitz_tbl1_248054281  |title=Chromosome numbers of the Malus wild species collection Dresden Pillnitz  }}
</ref>

== Description ==
It reaches from between {{Convert|3 and 8|m|frac=2}} tall and bears white flowers and yellow or red fruit.<ref name="foc" />

== Taxonomy ==
It was described botanically by [[Carl Ludwig Willdenow|Willdenow]] in the genus ''[[Pyrus]]'' and was transferred to ''Malus'' in 1803.<ref>[http://ipni.org] [[International Plant Names Index|The International Plant Names Index]]</ref>

=== Varieties ===
''Malus prunifolia'' has at least four varieties, some are grown for their fruit:<ref name=hort/><ref>{{ cite web |url=http://www.tropicos.org/NameSearch.aspx?name=Malus+prunifolia |title=Name Search: Malus prunifolia |work=Tropicos |publisher=[[Missouri Botanical Garden]] |location= [[St. Louis, Missouri]] |access-date=September 11, 2009}}</ref><ref>{{ cite web |url=http://www.plantnames.unimelb.edu.au/Sorting/Malus.html |title=Sorting Malus names |author=Michel H. Porcher |work=Multilingual Multiscript Plant Name Database |publisher=[[University of Melbourne]] |date=May 10, 2005 |access-date=September 11, 2009}}</ref>

* ''Malus prunifolia'' var. ''obliquipedicellata'' <small>X.W. Li & J.W. Sun</small>
* ''M. prunifolia'' var. ''prunifolia''
* ''M. prunifolia'' var. ''ringo'' <small>Asami</small> (Chinese apple)
* ''M. prunifolia'' var. ''rinki'' <small>(Koidz.) Rehder P.L.Wilson</small> (plum-leaf or Chinese crabapple)

== Distribution and habitat ==
''Malus prunifolia'' is found in China in the provinces of [[Gansu]], [[Guizhou]], [[Hebei]], [[Henan]], [[Liaoning]], [[Nei Mongol]], [[Qinghai]], [[Shaanxi]], [[Shandong]], [[Shanxi]], and possibly<!-- FoC shows it as "?Xinjiang" --> [[Xinjiang]]. It is adapted to grow at a variety of elevations from sea-level plains, to slopes as high as {{Convert|1300|m|abbr=on}}.<ref name="foc" />

== Uses ==
Outside of China, it is grown for use as an [[ornamental plant|ornamental tree]] or as [[rootstock]].{{Citation needed|date=December 2024}}
